questions.prompt: On this T1-weighted MRI of the head and neck, click the brain.
questions.hint: The large organ filling the cranial cavity.
questions.explain: The brain comprises the cerebrum, cerebellum and brainstem within the skull. On T1 white matter is brighter than grey matter, and CSF is dark.

questions.prompt: On this T1-weighted MRI of the head and neck, click the vertebrae.
questions.hint: The stack of bones forming the spinal column behind the airway.
questions.explain: The vertebrae form the spinal column and enclose the spinal canal. On T1 the vertebral body marrow is bright because of fat.

questions.prompt: On this T1-weighted MRI of the head and neck, click the lung.
questions.hint: Air-filled tissue at the lower edge of the field of view.
questions.explain: The lung apices rise above the first rib into the base of the neck. On T1 the lungs are very dark because they contain mostly air.

questions.prompt: A 30-year-old man has neck pain, tingling in both hands and progressive weakness after a diving accident. On this T1-weighted MRI, click the structure inside the spinal canal that carries nerve fibres from the brain.
questions.hint: It sits within the vertebral canal, surrounded by CSF.
questions.explain: The spinal cord runs within the vertebral canal and is injured by trauma or compression. On T1 it is intermediate in signal, surrounded by dark CSF.
